evals.prompt: Reskin the primary palette to a deeper blue (around 220 hue, 95% saturation, contrast threshold 60) by editing the app's stylesheet. Do not touch any other palette.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies the project as webforJ 25 and prior, edits the project's existing app stylesheet and overrides the primary palette config tokens at `:root`. It uses the three webforJ 25 palette config variables `--dwc-color-primary-h`, `--dwc-color-primary-s`, and `--dwc-color-primary-c` with the requested values. It validates the generated CSS via `webforj-mcp:styles_validate_tokens` with the resolved version before declaring done.
expectations: Resolves the target webforJ version from `pom.xml` as `25.10` (or `25.x` major) and routes the work as a webforJ 25 task
Edits the project's existing app stylesheet (or creates a new one inside the project's existing CSS load mechanism, NOT inventing a new wiring path)

Overrides ONLY the primary palette at `:root` using `--dwc-color-primary-h`, `--dwc-color-primary-s`, AND `--dwc-color-primary-c` (the contrast-threshold token is documented for webforJ 25 and the prompt explicitly asks for it)
Sets `--dwc-color-primary-c` to a numeric value in the range 0-100 (the prompt specifies 60)
Does NOT introduce `--dwc-color-primary-seed` for this webforJ 25 task (`-seed` is documented in webforJ 26+ only)
Calls `webforj-mcp:styles_validate_tokens` with the resolved `webforjVersion` and the generated CSS content before declaring the task done
Does NOT hardcode any raw hex / rgb / hsl color in the stylesheet (palette config tokens only)
Does NOT modify other palettes (`success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`, `default`, `gray`)

evals.prompt: Set the primary brand color to `#6366f1` exactly (no hue/saturation conversion). Then add a custom dark theme called `corporate-dark` that uses the same brand color.
evals.expected_output: The agent identifies the project as webforJ 26 and later, uses `--dwc-color-primary-seed` at `:root` for the exact color, and adds a custom dark theme via `html[data-app-theme='corporate-dark']` with `--dwc-dark-mode: 1`, `color-scheme: dark`, and the same seed. It validates the generated CSS via the MCP tool with the resolved version.
expectations: Resolves the target webforJ version from `pom.xml` as `26.00` (or `26.x` major) and routes the work as a webforJ 26+ task
Sets `--dwc-color-primary-seed: #6366f1` at `:root` (the documented direct-color override in webforJ 26+)
Defines the custom theme with the exact selector form `html[data-app-theme='corporate-dark']` (or `html[data-app-theme="corporate-dark"]`)
Inside the custom-dark selector, sets BOTH `--dwc-dark-mode: 1` AND `color-scheme: dark` (the two flags webforJ 26+ requires to make a custom theme dark)
Reuses the same `#6366f1` brand color inside the custom-dark theme (via the seed token, NOT by re-deriving hue/saturation)
Does NOT introduce `--dwc-color-primary-c` (the contrast-threshold token does not exist in webforJ 26+)
Calls `webforj-mcp:styles_validate_tokens` with the resolved `webforjVersion` and the generated CSS before declaring the task done
Does NOT hardcode `#6366f1` outside the seed assignment (no raw color inside component styles)

evals.prompt: Override the background of `dwc-button` to use a muted shade from the primary palette across the whole app.
evals.expected_output: The agent first calls `webforj-mcp:styles_get_component` with `webforjVersion: "26.00"` and `name: 'dwc-button'` (or `'Button'`) to look up the real CSS variables exposed by the component for that version. It writes a CSS rule on the `dwc-button` tag selector that sets `--dwc-button-background` to a `var(--dwc-color-*)` reference (NOT a raw hex). It then validates the CSS via `webforj-mcp:styles_validate_tokens` with the same `webforjVersion`.
expectations: Calls `webforj-mcp:styles_get_component` with `webforjVersion: "26.00"` (the full major.minor string, NOT bare `"26"`) and `name: 'Button'` or `name: 'dwc-button'` BEFORE writing the CSS
Passes a non-empty `reasoning` string to every styling-MCP tool call (it is required by the augmented-fields contract)
The generated CSS sets `--dwc-button-background` inside a `dwc-button { ... }` rule (or equivalent tag-scoped selector)
The value of `--dwc-button-background` is a `var(--dwc-color-*)` reference, NOT a raw hex / rgb / hsl color
Calls `webforj-mcp:styles_validate_tokens` with `webforjVersion: "26.00"` and the generated CSS content before declaring the task done
Does NOT use `::part()` for setting the background, since `--dwc-button-background` is a documented CSS variable on the component

evals.prompt: I want the dark theme to use a softer green for success messages. Don't add a new theme.
evals.expected_output: The agent honors the no-new-theme constraint and the skill's preference for overriding built-in themes. It overrides `html[data-app-theme="dark"]` (the documented dark-theme selector) with `--dwc-color-success-h` and `--dwc-color-success-s` (or `--dwc-color-success-seed`) for a softer green. It does NOT introduce a new `html[data-app-theme='your-name']` custom theme. It validates the generated CSS via MCP.
expectations: Resolves the target webforJ version as `26.00` (webforJ 26+)
Modifies the success palette inside `html[data-app-theme="dark"] { ... }` (the documented selector for overriding the built-in dark theme), NOT inside `:root`
Sets `--dwc-color-success-h` and `--dwc-color-success-s` (or `--dwc-color-success-seed`) — palette config tokens, NOT raw hex colors
Does NOT introduce a new custom theme via `html[data-app-theme='soft-success']` or any other novel `data-app-theme` value (the prompt explicitly forbids it)
Does NOT introduce `--dwc-color-success-c` (webforJ 26+ has no `-c`)
Does NOT modify any palette other than `success`
Calls `webforj-mcp:styles_validate_tokens` with `webforjVersion: "26.00"` and the generated CSS

evals.prompt: Add a new utility class `.section-pad` that gives a section roughly 24 px of padding all around. Edit the app stylesheet.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses a `--dwc-space-*` token instead of hardcoding `24px`. It calls `webforj-mcp:styles_list_tokens` with `prefix: --dwc-space-` to see the available spacing tokens for the version, picks the closest one, writes the rule, and validates.
expectations: Calls `webforj-mcp:styles_list_tokens` with `webforjVersion: "26.00"` and `prefix: "--dwc-space-"` (or equivalently broad enough to return spacing tokens) BEFORE writing the rule
The generated `.section-pad` rule uses `padding: var(--dwc-space-*)` with a real spacing token name returned by the MCP tool, NOT a hardcoded `24px`
Does NOT hardcode any raw `px`, `rem`, or `em` length in the new rule
Calls `webforj-mcp:styles_validate_tokens` with the generated CSS before declaring the task done
Does NOT invent a non-existent spacing token (any `--dwc-space-*` name MUST be one returned by `styles_list_tokens`)

evals.prompt: Change the visual appearance of an element inside the `dwc-table` shadow DOM that has no exposed CSS variable for it (for example, the styling of a specific cell or row part).
evals.expected_output: The agent calls `webforj-mcp:styles_get_component` for `dwc-table` with `webforjVersion: "26.00"`, sees that `dwc-table` exposes shadow parts but no CSS variable for the requested visual, and writes a `dwc-table::part(...)` rule using a part name returned by the MCP tool. The generated CSS uses DWC tokens (e.g. `var(--dwc-color-*)`) for any color values and avoids any forbidden sizing properties on table parts.
expectations: Calls `webforj-mcp:styles_get_component` with `webforjVersion: "26.00"` and `name: 'dwc-table'` BEFORE writing CSS
Uses `dwc-table::part(<name>)` with a part name returned by the MCP tool (no invented part names)
Any color value inside the rule references a `--dwc-color-*` token via `var(...)`, NOT a raw hex
Does NOT set `height`, `padding`, `margin`, `min-height`, `max-height`, `line-height`, or `width` on a table part (table sizing is managed by Java APIs)
Calls `webforj-mcp:styles_validate_tokens` with the generated CSS before declaring the task done

evals.prompt: Reskin my app to use this primary brand color: HSL(220, 70%, 50%). I want it to apply across the whole app.
evals.expected_output: On webforJ 26+, the seed system regenerates all 19 shades, semantic variations, text-contrast tokens, borders, and focus rings from a single seed color. The canonical solution is a one-line `--dwc-color-primary-seed: hsl(220, 70%, 50%)` at `:root` (or, equivalently, `--dwc-color-primary-h: 220` + `--dwc-color-primary-s: 70%`). Calling `webforj-mcp:create_theme` with `primaryColor: [220, 70, 50]` is also acceptable. What is NOT acceptable: hand-rolling variation tokens, or hardcoding a hex color anywhere outside the seed assignment.
expectations: Resolves the target webforJ version from `pom.xml` as `26.00` (webforJ 26+)

Produces a reskin that uses ONE of these documented approaches: (a) `--dwc-color-primary-seed: hsl(220, 70%, 50%)` at `:root`, OR (b) `--dwc-color-primary-h: 220` and `--dwc-color-primary-s: 70%` at `:root`, OR (c) a `webforj-mcp:create_theme` call with `webforjVersion: "26.00"` and `primaryColor: [220, 70, 50]`
Does NOT hand-write variation tokens (`--dwc-color-primary-dark`, `--dwc-color-primary-light`, `--dwc-color-primary-text-*`, etc.) when the seed or `-h`/`-s` regenerates them automatically
Does NOT hardcode a raw hex / rgb / hsl color anywhere outside the seed assignment (the only place a literal color is allowed is the seed itself)
Does NOT introduce `--dwc-color-primary-c` (webforJ 26+ has no `-c`)
Calls `webforj-mcp:styles_validate_tokens` with `webforjVersion: "26.00"` and the generated CSS before declaring the task done

evals.prompt: Mark overdue rows in a `dwc-table` with a red background.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses the documented part-provider mechanism: a Java `setRowPartProvider` returns a part name like `"row-overdue"` for matching rows. CSS targets `dwc-table::part(row-overdue)` and uses a `var(--dwc-color-danger-*)` token for the red background. The agent does not set forbidden sizing properties on the table part and validates the CSS.
expectations: Adds Java code that calls `table.setRowPartProvider(...)` returning a `List<String>` containing a part name (e.g. `"row-overdue"`) when the row matches the overdue condition, otherwise an empty list
Adds a CSS rule `dwc-table::part(row-overdue) { ... }` (or whatever part name the Java code returned)
The CSS rule's color uses a `var(--dwc-color-danger-*)` token (e.g. `--dwc-color-danger`, `--dwc-color-danger-alt`), NOT a raw hex / rgb / hsl
Does NOT set `height`, `padding`, `margin`, `min-height`, `max-height`, `line-height`, or `width` on the table part
Calls `webforj-mcp:styles_validate_tokens` with the generated CSS before declaring the task done
Does NOT recreate row-coloring logic in CSS via attribute selectors when the documented mechanism is the Java part provider

evals.prompt: Make the theme follow the user's operating system preference: 'light' for light mode, 'dark-pure' for dark mode.
evals.expected_output: The agent annotates the App class with `@AppTheme("system")` plus `@AppDarkTheme("dark-pure")` to override the default dark-slot theme. `@AppLightTheme` is NOT added because `light` is already the default for the light slot. webforJ resolves `system` to the registered light or dark theme at runtime and re-resolves when the OS preference changes. The agent does NOT write per-theme CSS overrides for this task because the two existing built-in themes already cover the requirement.
expectations: Adds `@AppTheme("system")` to the App class
Adds `@AppDarkTheme("dark-pure")` to override the dark-slot default (`@AppDarkTheme` defaults to `dark`, not `dark-pure`)
Does NOT add a redundant `@AppLightTheme("light")` — `@AppLightTheme` already defaults to `light`, so this annotation is only needed when the desired light-slot theme is something else
Does NOT call `App.setTheme("light")` or `App.setTheme("dark-pure")` imperatively (annotations cover this)
Does NOT introduce a new custom theme via `html[data-app-theme='...']` (the built-in `light` and `dark-pure` cover both cases)
Does NOT hardcode any raw color in CSS for this task

evals.prompt: Make every component inside the `.admin-section` wrapper use a red primary palette. The rest of the app must keep its existing primary color.
evals.expected_output: The agent writes a section-scoped override: a single rule on `.admin-section` that sets `--dwc-color-primary-seed` (or `--dwc-color-primary-h`/`-s`). CSS custom properties cascade, so everything inside the wrapper retunes automatically. The agent does NOT touch `:root` or any `html[data-app-theme="..."]` selector.
expectations: Generates a rule scoped to `.admin-section` (or an equivalent wrapper class/id) that sets `--dwc-color-primary-seed`, OR `--dwc-color-primary-h` and `--dwc-color-primary-s`, with a red value
Does NOT modify `:root` to retune the primary palette
Does NOT modify any `html[data-app-theme="..."]` selector to retune the primary palette
Does NOT manually override individual variation tokens (`--dwc-color-primary-dark`, `--dwc-color-primary-light`, etc.) — the seed regenerates them
Does NOT hardcode the red as a raw color on individual components inside `.admin-section`
Calls `webforj-mcp:styles_validate_tokens` with `webforjVersion: "26.00"` and the generated CSS

evals.prompt: I want a `.status-badge` class that shows the primary palette as its background. The same CSS rule should produce a sensible color in both light and dark modes without me writing two rules.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses a variation token (`var(--dwc-color-primary)`) — variations resolve to a different step in light vs dark mode automatically. The agent does NOT use a raw step number (`var(--dwc-color-primary-50)`) because raw steps freeze at the same OKLCH lightness in both modes.
expectations: The `.status-badge` rule sets `background` to `var(--dwc-color-primary)` (the variation token), NOT a raw palette step like `var(--dwc-color-primary-50)`
Does NOT add a second rule scoped under `html[data-app-theme="dark"]` for `.status-badge` — the variation token already adapts
Does NOT hardcode a raw hex / rgb / hsl color
Calls `webforj-mcp:styles_validate_tokens` with `webforjVersion: "26.00"` and the generated CSS

evals.prompt: I have a Button instance called `delete` that needs to look like a danger action. Don't write custom CSS — use the component's built-in styling.
evals.expected_output: The agent reaches for the component's typed semantic-theme setter, NOT custom CSS. It calls `delete.setTheme(ButtonTheme.DANGER)`. The semantic palette already covers `danger`, so no styling code is required.
expectations: Sets the button's theme to `ButtonTheme.DANGER` via the typed setter `delete.setTheme(ButtonTheme.DANGER)`
Does NOT call `delete.setAttribute("theme", "danger")` — webforJ components do not expose `setAttribute` for component-level styling
Does NOT write any custom CSS for the button (no `dwc-button { ... }` rule, no `--dwc-button-background` override, no inline style)
Does NOT introduce a new custom theme via `html[data-app-theme='...']`
Does NOT hardcode a red color anywhere

evals.prompt: I'm building a row of three form controls: a TextField, a ComboBox, and a Button. The user wants all three to be visually aligned at the 'large' size.
evals.expected_output: The agent calls the typed setter `setExpanse(Expanse.LARGE)` on each of the three controls. Expanse unifies height and font size across controls so they line up exactly; the agent does NOT set explicit width/height/font-size on each control to fake it.
expectations: Calls `setExpanse(Expanse.LARGE)` on EACH of the three controls (TextField, ComboBox, Button)
Does NOT call `setAttribute("expanse", "l")` — webforJ components do not expose `setAttribute` for sizing
Uses webforJ Java syntax — no BBj `setAttribute(...)` on `web!` or `field!`, no `BBjEditBox`, etc.
Does NOT set `width`, `height`, `font-size`, or `--dwc-size-*` overrides on the controls to simulate sizing manually
Does NOT write CSS for sizing — the expanse attribute is the documented mechanism

evals.prompt: I'm building a custom callout component. It has a primary-color background with a label of text directly on top. Both the background and the label color must stay readable in both light and dark mode.
evals.expected_output: The agent uses two semantically correct webforJ 26+ tokens: `--dwc-color-primary` for the background (the variation, mode-adaptive) and `--dwc-color-on-primary-text` for the text on top of the colored background (auto-contrast, WCAG AA, clamped per shade). It does NOT use `--dwc-color-primary-text` for the foreground, because in v2 that token is surface-safe text intended for use on neutral page backgrounds — not on a colored fill.
expectations: Sets `background` (or `background-color`) to `var(--dwc-color-primary)`
Sets `color` for the label text on top of that background to `var(--dwc-color-on-primary-text)` (the `on-{name}-text` variation, the documented webforJ 26+ token for text placed ON a colored shade)
Does NOT use `var(--dwc-color-primary-text)` as the label color — that token is for colored text on neutral surfaces, not for text on a colored fill
Does NOT hardcode `#ffffff` / `white` / `#000000` / `black` as the label color
Calls `webforj-mcp:styles_validate_tokens` with `webforjVersion: "26.00"` and the generated CSS
